searchArea: Search any city, town or locality in India

tapMap: Tap anywhere on the map to check that exact spot
allClear: No place is at high risk right now.
whyNote: The reasons below are shown in English.
reportTitle: Is there water on your street now?
reportNote: Your report shows on the map for 48 hours. It stores the spot and the depth, nothing about you.
reportThanks: Thank you. Your neighbours can see it now.
noReports: No reports near here in the last 48 hours.
trackTitle: How good has the forecast been here?
trackIntro: Each day, the rain forecast a day ahead for this spot against the rain that fell.
heavyDays: Days of heavy rain or more
heavyNone: No heavy rain fell here in this period, so the forecast has not been tested on the days that matter most.
reservoirsIntro: A release raises the river whether or not it is raining. Chennai Metro Water, as on
streetAlertTitle: Tell me when this street is at risk
streetAlertText: One email when this street reaches High, and when risk appears in the places Vellam watches. The street is stored without your address.
terrainIntro: Real ground heights and buildings. Blue dots are streets residents marked as flooded in December 2015.
spotDry: This spot would stay above the water by
spotUnder: This spot would be under water by
shareUnder: of this view would be under.
waterCaveat: This shows the shape of the ground. It is not a forecast. It floods everything below one height, as if the area were a bathtub; real floods follow drains, walls and rivers. Heights come from a satellite survey about 30 m across that includes rooftops.
higherIntro: Roads within 1.2 km that are at least 2 m higher than this spot and clear of streets that flooded in 2015.
higherNone: No clearly higher road was found within 1.2 km.
higherCaveat: These come from satellite height data, which can mistake a flyover or a rooftop for ground. Look at the place before you rely on it.
replayIntro: What Vellam would have said, given the rain that fell that day. This tests how it judges a place, not the forecast.
replayResultTitle: What the Michaung replay proves, and what it does not
prepareIntro: What each level means and what to do when your street reaches it.
alertsTitle: Get an email when flooding becomes likely
alertsText: One message when risk appears. Not one every three hours while it lasts.
helplinesIntro: Tap to call. Save them now, while the network works.
howNote: This page is shown in English.
footer: Vellam is a guide, not an official warning. Follow the India Meteorological Department and your local authority.
guideLOW: No flooding expected here in the next 48 hours
guideLOW1: Nothing to do now. Check again when the forecast changes.
guideWATCH: Water may collect on low streets here
guideWATCH1: Move vehicles out of basements and low parking spots.
guideWATCH2: Clear the drain outside your home if it is safe to do so.
guideWATCH4: Check on elderly neighbours and anyone living on a ground floor.
guideHIGH1: Move vehicles, documents and valuables to higher ground or an upper floor now.
guideHIGH2: Store drinking water and food for two days, and keep medicines within reach.
guideHIGH3: Stay out of basements, subways and underpasses.
guideHIGH4: Do not walk or ride through moving water.
guideHIGH5: Switch off the mains if water enters the house.
guideSEVERE1: Be ready to leave. Pack documents, medicines, drinking water, a torch and a charged phone.
guideSEVERE2: Move to an upper floor, or to a relief centre if water starts rising.
guideSEVERE3: Switch off electricity and gas before water reaches the sockets.
guideSEVERE4: Stay away from fallen power lines and electric poles.
guideSEVERE5: Call 112 if you or a neighbour need help.
searchNone: No place in India was found with that name.
coverage: Chennai has the deepest record: streets that flooded in 2015, mapped water bodies and reservoir releases. Everywhere else in India, Vellam uses the rain forecast, ground height and nearby water.
